title: TensorFlow Examples
description: Small TensorFlow examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Tensors hold numbers
examples.description: A tensor is a number container with a shape. It can be a single number, a list or a table.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([2, 4, 6])
print(x.numpy().tolist())

examples.title: Shape and rank
examples.description: Shape lists dimension sizes. Rank is the number of dimensions, not a score of model quality.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
print(x.shape, x.ndim)

examples.title: Choose the numeric type
examples.description: A dtype tells TensorFlow how to store tensor values. Many model computations use floating-point numbers.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([1, 2], dtype=tf.float32)
print(x.dtype.name)

examples.title: Tensor arithmetic
examples.description: Operators can work element by element on matching tensor shapes.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

a = tf.constant([1, 2])
b = tf.constant([3, 4])
print((a + b).numpy().tolist())

examples.title: Broadcast a scalar
examples.description: A scalar is a single value. Broadcasting can apply it across all positions of a tensor.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([2, 4, 6])
print((x * 2).numpy().tolist())

examples.title: Reduce to a summary
examples.description: A reduction combines values into a summary, such as a sum or mean.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([2.0, 4.0, 6.0])
print(float(tf.reduce_mean(x).numpy()))

examples.title: Reshape the same data
examples.description: reshape changes the arrangement while preserving the number of values.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.constant([1, 2, 3, 4])
print(tf.reshape(x, (2, 2)).numpy().tolist())

examples.title: Variables can change
examples.description: A TensorFlow Variable holds a value that can be updated. Model weights are usually stored in variables.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

count = tf.Variable(2.0)
count.assign_add(1.0)
print(float(count.numpy()))

examples.title: Gradients describe a local change
examples.description: A gradient describes how an output changes near the current input. GradientTape records operations so TensorFlow can calculate a derivative.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

x = tf.Variable(3.0)
with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
    y = x * x
print(float(tape.gradient(y, x).numpy()))

examples.title: A dense layer combines inputs
examples.description: A dense layer learns weights that combine input features. Here a layer with three units produces three values for each input row.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

layer = tf.keras.layers.Dense(3)
x = tf.constant([[1.0, 2.0]])
print(tuple(layer(x).shape))

examples.title: Train a tiny model
examples.description: Training adjusts weights to reduce a loss, which measures mistakes. This toy example fits numbers near a simple doubling rule.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

import numpy as np
x = np.array([[1.], [2.], [3.], [4.]], dtype="float32")
y = np.array([[2.], [4.], [6.], [8.]], dtype="float32")
model = tf.keras.Sequential([tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,)), tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)])
model.compile(optimizer="sgd", loss="mse")
model.fit(x, y, epochs=20, verbose=0)
print(tuple(model(x).shape))

examples.title: Save an untrained model carefully
examples.description: Keras can save a model to a .keras file. Saving preserves a model; it does not improve its accuracy.
examples.code:
import tensorflow as tf

model = tf.keras.Sequential([tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,)), tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)])
model.save("practice-model.keras")
